title: CDPHE public health data catalog — schema
description: Schema for the discovery-phase data catalog prototype. All catalog data lives in one public JSON file, data_sources.json, whose root is an array of records. Each record is one of three data product types (dataset, dashboard, summary_report), identified by its `type` field. Records are ordered by type (datasets, then dashboards, then summary reports) and alphabetically by name within each type; that order is a convention, not enforced here.

record.description: One catalog record. The `type` field decides which definition applies, and exactly one must match.

id.description: Stable, globally unique identifier for the record (GUID/UUID, lowercase, e.g. '3f2b8c1e-6d4a-5b7e-9c0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f'), used as the target of cross-references from related_* fields. Must not change once assigned.

id_ref.description: A reference to the `id` (GUID) of another record. Referential integrity (that the referenced id exists, and that links point both ways) is enforced by convention, not by this schema.

name.description: Plain-language name in sentence case. Includes the years for time-bound outputs, e.g. 'Suicide deaths, 2004–2025 (excludes race)'.

description.description: Plain-language summary of what the product contains and what questions it can help answer.

publisher.description: The organization that publishes the product: 'CDPHE', or the name of an outside organization.

topics.description: Public health topics this product is primarily about, used for search and filtering. Tag the product's main subjects, not everything it mentions: a survey that asks one question about vaccines is not tagged 'Vaccines'. Overlapping topics are fine when both apply (e.g. HIV data gets 'Sexual health' and 'Communicable disease'). By convention, list the most relevant topic first. Files that are one slice of a larger survey (one year, region or breakdown) get only the survey's main topic; the survey's own record carries its full set.

population.description: Every age group the product covers, used by the Population filter. Values are age ranges in years: '<1' (infants), '1-17' (children), '18-64' (adults) and '65+' (older adults). Tag a group when any part of the product's age range falls in it: for example, ages 15–19 gets both '1-17' and '18-64'. A product covering all ages lists all four. By convention, list values youngest to oldest.

geographic_level.description: Every geographic level the product is published at (e.g. ['state', 'county']). 'region' is only for groupings that are not Health Statistics Regions (for example, Denver metro / other metro / rural). The explorer shows 'health_statistics_region' as 'Region' and 'census_tract' as 'Census tract'.

last_updated.description: Date the product or its underlying data was last refreshed, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). Only set when the source states it.

update_frequency.description: How often newer data of this kind appears. It describes the data, not the product: a dashboard that refreshes monthly but shows yearly data is 'annual'. For one edition of a recurring series (an annual report, a birth cohort file), use the series' cadence while the series is running, even though that edition won't change. 'weekly', 'monthly', 'quarterly', 'semiannual' (twice a year), 'annual' and 'biennial' (every two years) are regular schedules. Data collected only during part of the year uses its cadence during that period; say when collection happens in the description (e.g. 'Collected weekly from May 1 to September 30'). 'irregular': updated, but on no fixed schedule. 'one_time': a standalone publication that was never part of a series and won't be updated. 'discontinued': the series or program used to produce this data and has stopped. null: unknown. Use null rather than a guess.

successor_id.description: id of the record that supersedes this one: the next edition in the same series (the 2024 report for the 2023 report), or a different product that replaced a discontinued one, when a source says so. Points to the immediate next edition, not the latest; follow the chain to reach the newest. Null or omitted when no successor is in the catalog, including when the next edition is expected but not yet published. If a newer edition is published but missing from the catalog, add it as a record and link it. By convention, not enforced here: the target exists and covers later years, a record can't be its own successor, no record is the successor of more than one record, and chains don't loop. The reverse link (what this record replaced) is derived, not stored.

years_covered.description: Calendar years the product covers, as four-digit years listed individually so gaps are explicit and filtering by year works (e.g. [2018, 2019, 2020]). School years and seasons (e.g. 2023–24) list both calendar years.

link.description: Primary public URL for the product (dataset landing page, report, or dashboard). Must be publicly accessible.

documentation.description: Public URL to data documentation, a data dictionary, or methodology. Null if none. Change to an array of URLs if multiple documents apply.

contact.description: Public contact email address for questions about this product. Null if none is available yet; the UI still shows a contact control in that case so staff can see none is available.

dataset.description: Data product: a source data program (survey, registry, surveillance system) or a downloadable, analysis-ready data file, data portal layer, or query tool.

short_name.description: Abbreviated name or acronym for compact display (e.g. 'BRFSS').

related_dashboards.description: ids of dashboards built on or related to this dataset.

related_reports.description: ids of summary reports built on or related to this dataset.

dashboard.description: Data product: an interactive dashboard (e.g. Tableau, Shiny or ArcGIS) built on one or more datasets.

related_datasets.description: ids of datasets this dashboard is based on or related to.

summary_report.description: Data product: aggregate data published as a fixed file or page, such as a spreadsheet of summary tables, a PDF report, or tables on a web page.

related_datasets.description: ids of datasets this report is based on or related to.
